properties.areaDesc: Central Coast of Oregon
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 7 at 12:35PM PST until November 8 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement on the beaches, sneaker
waves possible. For the High Surf Advisory on the beaches, large
sneaker waves and hazardous surf conditions. Breakers up to 28
feet.

* WHERE...Central Coast of Oregon.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through late tonight.
For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 AM to 10 PM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties,
and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off
rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Minor
beach erosion may damage coastal properties and buildings.
Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-
lying shoreline. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people off
of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Caution should be used when in or near
the water, especially those who will be razor clamming. Keep
children and pets away from the surf zone. Keep off of
jetties, rocks and logs near the surf zone. If you see someone
swept into the sea do not swim in after them. Call 911 and
keep an eye on them until help arrives.
properties.instruction:
A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can easily lift or roll logs which can injure or kill
someone caught in their path.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 7 at 11:34AM CST until November 9 at 9:00AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
Multiple rounds of locally heavy rainfall are expected between
Saturday night and early Monday morning across the Rio Grande Plains
and Brush Country.  The first round is most likely between midnight
and mid-morning Sunday, when 1 to 2 inches with locally 3 or more
inches of rain may fall. The second round is expected Sunday night
into early Monday morning, when an additional 1 to 3 inches with
locally 4 inches or more may fall.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Deep South Texas, including the following
counties, Brooks, Jim Hogg and Zapata.

* WHEN...From 6 PM CST this evening through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of arroyos and
streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Some
arroyos may rise out of their banks near where heaviest rains fall.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Storm drains
and ditches may become clogged with debris. Highest concern
includes locations in Zapata, such as Medina Addition, as well as
more populated areas of Hebbronville and Falfurrias, including
along state highways 16, 359, and 285.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Potential for heavy rainfall, including two windows where
rainfall rates could reach 2 inches per hour for two hours both
late tonight and early Sunday morning, and again Sunday night
through mid morning Monday.
- Concern is highest across populated areas, including the cities
of Zapata, Hebbronville, and Falfurrias.  Flood prone areas along
or near arroyos in Jim Hogg and Zapata are at most risk, but high
water could also flood open rangeland.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued November 6 at 3:14PM PST until November 7 at 6:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
...RISK FOR RAPID FIRE GROWTH AND EXTREME FIRE BEHAVIOR WITH ANY
NEW FIRE STARTS, ESPECIALLY LATE TONIGHT THROUGH SATURDAY...

.Weak to moderate Santa Ana winds will be on the increase,
peaking on Saturday. During the peak, gusts of 30 to 45 mph will
be common in the typical wind-prone areas of Los Angeles and
Ventura Counties. Meanwhile, the air will warm and dry, with
minimum humidities in the 8 to 20 percent range common by
Saturday. Fuels remain critically dry despite some minor greenup
from recent rains. There is a high risk for fast-moving fires
where the plants are driest and the winds are strongest, which
this targeted Red Flag Warning addresses.

* AFFECTED AREA...Santa Clarita Valley, Western Santa Monica
Mountains Recreational Area, Eastern Santa Monica Mountains
Recreational Area, Santa Susana Mountains and Western San
Gabriel Mountains and Highway 14 Corridor.

* TIMING...From 2 AM to 6 PM PST Saturday.

* WINDS...Northeast 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 45 mph.
Isolated gusts 45 to 55 mph in most favored locations.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Minimums of 8 to 20 percent. Poor
overnight recoveries.

* IMPACTS...If fire ignition occurs, conditions are favorable
for extreme fire behavior which would threaten life and
property.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. Use extreme caution
with anything that can spark a wildfire. Residents near wildland
interfaces should be prepared to evacuate if a wildfire breaks
out. See readyforwildfire.org and wildfirerisk.org for
information.

surf up to 4 to 6 feet expected. Surf will likely increase
around Monday for the Ventura Coasts.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Santa Barbara
County Southwestern Coast, Santa Barbara County Southeastern
Coast, Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles
County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore. Pooling of sea water is possible around high tide
at beach and harbor areas that is uncommon with normal tidal
ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is also possible.

expected each morning. Surf and coastal flooding impacts peak on
Monday, when a High Surf Advisory and Coastal Flood Advisory is
likely to be issued for the Ventura Coasts. For the remainder of
the coasts, it is possible that a Coastal Flood Advisory is
needed for Monday as well.

stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
